title: test_port_limits fetches then immediately discards two tier_index results (basic, std)
evidence:
basic, _ := tier_index(cat, "standard")
	_ = basic
	// spawn a basic router + 5 houses in span
	rt, _ := node_type_index(cat, "router_basic")
	res, _ := node_type_index(cat, "residential")
	rid := spawn_node(&state.topology, rt, {20, 20}, 0, cat)
	std, _ := tier_index(cat, "standard")
	wide, _ := tier_index(cat, "wide")
	_ = std
detail: basic and std each bind tier_index("standard") then are discarded via `_ =`; only wide is used. basic is also misnamed — it is a pipe-tier index, not the router_basic the surrounding comment references (a separate `basic` at line 239 IS the router index), which will confuse readers.
recommended_fix: Delete the `basic, _ := ...` / `_ = basic` and `std, _ := ...` / `_ = std` lines; keep only the `wide` binding (the tier the loop actually draws).

title: severance_fixture discards the drawn leg's Edit_Result, then tests hardcode the pipe id as u32(2)
evidence:
direct, _ := topology_apply_edit(&state.topology,
		Command{kind = Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = router, b = h1, tier = std}}, cat, state.inventory, 1)
	state.director.growth_done = 1 << 30
	if with_alt {
		j2 := spawn_node(&state.topology, mid_t, {14, 16}, 0, cat)
		submit_c(state, Command{kind = Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = router, b = j2, tier = std}}, 0)
		submit_c(state, Command{kind = Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = j2, b = h1, tier = std}}, 0)
	}
	_ = direct
...
	direct := u32(2)
detail: The fixture draws the router→h1 leg into `direct` (an Edit_Result whose .pipe is the real id) then throws it away; both severance tests instead hardcode `direct := u32(2)`, silently coupling to draw order / next_pipe_id==1. Reordering the fixture draws breaks the demolish target with no compile signal.
recommended_fix: Have severance_fixture return direct.pipe (or accept it via an out-param) and pass that id into the Cmd_Demolish instead of the literal u32(2).
